free to use isn't the same as free to sell a copy of.

Wwise the sound engine component of the Crytek SDK is not free and comes with an evaluation license, you have to purchase a commercial license if you have more than 200 sound files and or you want to sell a commercial product that uses it. There is a limited commercial license available for free from the Wwise developers but that requires their approval and as the name implies has a few limitations like the same 200 sound file limit, no plugin support, and an expiration date (you can resubmit for a new limited license for free but they will review your project again) and if they decide not to renew your limited license then you could end up owing them quite a bit of money if you game ends up a selling.

The Wwise business model isn't as aggressive as I've made it sound, everyone involved in the CryTek SDK package wants indie devs, hobbyists, industry veterans skilling up /diversifying skillset to get everything they need to make a game and I've never heard of the company behind Wwise being shitheads to any indie dev but they are well within their rights to demand you pay for using their tools when you start making money off it and to be fair at that stage you're a small / medium business and should be crossing your t's and dotting your i's to make sure none of this bites you in the ass.

It says 'No Royalties' alright but 5 minutes of investigating and you can find out just how far that goes, strip out the Wwise components and I think its completely royalty free for commercial projects but you'd want to really be tied to CryTek SDK first and a lot of indie devs just arn't right now.
